title: What are the pros of knowing code while doing AI gamedev?
author: ElioVibe
selftext:
I've never vibecoded a whole project so I just have assumptions. I prefere let people who have more experience answer.

Please don't answer if like me you have just assumptions. I'd like opinions from people who did big projects, with or without knowing how to code

comments.author: IdealEmpty8363
comments.body: You will not struggle with the architecture when your game grows

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body:
Even being a beginner at coding will help and significantly enhance possibilities or it's almost useless below an advanced level ?

And a concrete exemple of the struggle you mean  tested to architecture would help. I'm still a noob

replies.author: count023
replies.body: if oyu know your patterns, like factory patterns, event handlers, singletons, etc... even as a beginner you are leagues ahead of hte people who are single prompting, "make me GTA 6" then it all breaks down trying to add new features.

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body: I'd knowing basic stuff like loops, condition, Mathf in unity, vector3 functions, etc .. Also very useful ?

replies.author: count023
replies.body: better than most, but learning software development patterns would be your priority in this case whether you were using an AI or not anyway.

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body: Cool. Could you gimme your list in what I should focus on? (I already know basic coding and I use Unity)

replies.author: count023
replies.body:
Honestly, start here: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software\_design\_pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_design_pattern)

That'll explain what i'm talking about and the principles why.

and this guy is great for breaking down each of them into practical examples of how/why to use htem:  
[https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns](https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns)

It's pretty much an industry standard, gaming or enterprise or anything really. There are acutal paid books that help but i try to aim people at free resources instead just so they aren't sinking money into a hobby.

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body:
Thank you. This should be highly valuable skill even in a decade?

Becayse in really sick of learning new things that become useless after 2 years since 2023 .. I've learn drawing, voice acting, 3D, now coding ... Every time I hear "There's no job for beginners anymore and in few years it should be even worse and the job. could disappear".

I have a disability so I can only work on a computer. I try to find smth at least a bit solid in the long run .. thank you for your help ..

replies.author: count023
replies.body: absolutly, software patterns haven't changed in about 30 years. they moved from "functional" to "object oriented" but that's about it, so yes, tehse skills will be viable for a long time. In fact, tehy'll more easily transfer than you think. If you know patterns and you jump companies or even roles, the languages cna change but the principle of how the code should function together will remain the same. and since hte AI now abstracts away the language part, it's the most valuable way you can learn right now is \_how\_ programs should be written and slot together as opposed to how to code with a specific language and you'll be set over all the other vibe coders today.

comments.author: Winter-Mix-5155
comments.body: L'avantage c'est de continuer d'apprendre en lisant la source qui a été pindu par l'IA parfois c'est surprenant...

comments.author: Kindly_Life_947
comments.body:
knowing code and understanding software engineering is different things. Knowing code and its syntax is the part that is being automated. Knowing the syntax of the code helps you if you have to fix things manually, but you really don't need it if you have quota left.

Knowing Software engineering and mathematics help you guide the AI to better solutions

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body:
And if we compare:
1. an amateur coder that simply knows stuff like classes, objects, conditions, loops, method, variables, unity methods, etc ..
2. Someone who doesn't know anything about coding.

Does the 1st one can produce significantly more complex games than the 2nd or almost no difference?

replies.author: Kindly_Life_947
replies.body: those are only the stuff that you need to make the code compile. It's not enough information to overcome AI weaknesses. Which is in understanding different approaches to solutions and to recognize when there is a better alternative.

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body:
But you didn't clearly answer the question.

So you'd say someone who knows the syntax of the language have 0 advantage compared to a pure cube coder that don't even know what a condition is?

And this even for a big project?

replies.author: Kindly_Life_947
replies.body:
Well I explained. Direct answer is minimal if non existent. It will help you read the code and understand it. So you are not totally in trouble if things go south or you run out of tokens, also it might help you save some tokens by not using AI to fix simple things like field rename etc, but with AI, things don't go south because it doesn't understand what those things like classes and objects are.   
  
They go south because it didn't get proper instructions on the design, it picked something that fit the current situation but then things started to change and new requirements came. They go south because it failed to understand that there is a lot more performant way to do the thing that is a good enough for the case etc.

replies.author: Kindly_Life_947
replies.body:
ok there is one thing that it will help you, but its not related to the application or game. It will help you understand programming, which is a doorway to better designs patterns, docs and optimizations. But that doesn't help if you don't want to learn anything else.

For a young person go ahead learn, but don't stop there like people use to. Learn design, test driven development and architecture. If I where a person who is starting and need to vibe code, I would first learn the theory and AI developed systems, then ask from AI what each code does and learn that way. 

You can try to write a simple program. Thats the best teacher but remember that takes a lot of time especially without AI

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body: Knowing how to read basic code,  what is a loop, etc .. is absolutely mandatory to learn pattern design no?

replies.author: Kindly_Life_947
replies.body:
if you are coding your self.   
  
Loop is a concept. just repeat this x number of times.  
You don't need to know the syntax. Just the math and this can be explained to the AI and AI can explain that in detail to you.

comments.author: More_Two_1105
comments.body:
Software engineers don't just write code. They are also involved in planning how to approach specific issues or requirements. 

Having a background in that field I think will help in planning how to approach and break up the project into manageable tasks, debug when there is an issue or look out for potential issues that the AI agent can cause while writing the code, like an approach that might hurt further down the line when scalibility becomes important or a change in how something needs to operate, when the model could be hallucinating or just bloating the code with unnessecary changes

comments.author: DisciplineBrave6808
comments.body:
First of all thanks for asking this question. Because everyone is just assuming there’s no good reason to know how to do things manually anymore. And we’re not there yet if ever. 

If you know game dev outside of ai you know what prompts to make and questions to ask. You know how to debug when things are wrong, which is currently still quite often. You also have a mind that allows you to innovate and you know how to push the boundaries and find the limitations of the ai.

comments.author: Level-Physics-1730
comments.body: person who knows will have a better entire experience across full development (assuming we aren't talking about a oneshot), the project itself while still being fully vibecoded with have a generalized "better than without the knowledge" feel/function to it.

comments.author: mechatui
comments.body: If you don’t know the technicals from engine stuff to code stuff right now it’s unlikely you will make a very good game and it will be a absolute mess to update, deploy etc

comments.author: olgalatepu
comments.body:
Knowing architecture design and data structures etc, is useful because AI will often try to translate specific commands into a solution as fast as possible delivering tangled and slow solutions. Probably because, eventually, they lack context.

Knowing code is useful to learn the former.

comments.author: Roma2443
comments.body:
I'm developer web and i'm making a multiplayer game with  help of ai, and i think my strenght is for the architecture i understand what i need to do, i understand what ai is doing i'm aware of optimisation i think i'm faster than a non-dev 

But it was yesterday ... today with model like astra i don't understand what my plus value is lol

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body: Did you test astra for long? You sure you don't have plus value compared to someone that don't knows what a loop is if you want to make a more advanced game than them?

replies.author: Roma2443
replies.body:
No i don't test astra bu i saw on reddit what people can achieve with it ... 

You don't need to know what a loop is anymore, if you really want to create an advanced game it will be possible right now for everyone with time but maybe too, a lot of token money

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body:
How do you explain that most of games here have very basic gameplay if AI fully replaces professional coders ?

Don't you think only professional coders can efficiently make these games more advanced?

replies.author: Roma2443
replies.body:
This is just my opinion. I’m not saying it’s a fact, but I think most of the games we see here are prototypes, where 80% of the work was done with AI in just a few days, while the remaining 20% could take years, even with AI. AI can help you with the code, but it doesn’t really help with the story, game design, or creating interesting gameplay loops.

Some people manage to stand out with a cool idea, simple but appealing graphics, and very basic code, while others use more advanced technologies but still don’t make games that feel appealing. At the same time, some passionate developers are already managing to create large, polished projects with AI despite having little or no prior knowledge.

We’re not seeing AA games being developed by a single person yet. AI still doesn’t replace a multidisciplinary team handling game design, programming, art direction, sound design, and so on. So we’re still a long way from replacing an entire game development team.

That’s why I agree with you that, for now, only professionals can really push these games to a more advanced level. But every day, the limits of what AI can do are being pushed further and further.
